name: Hukumina
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct (Buru area); only Holle wordlists (Stokhof 1982) and survey atlases in Glottolog; no descriptive phonology exists that would state stress.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 2000. Defining speech communities on Buru Island: a look at both linguistic and non-linguistic factors. In C.E. Grimes (ed.), Spices from the East: papers in languages of eastern Indonesia, 73-103. Pacific Linguistics 503.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 7.4.3: 'The language of Hukumina is very distinct from Buru in intonation, lexicon and sound correspondences' -- no stress location.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 1995. Digging for the roots of language death in eastern Indonesia: the cases of Kayeli and Hukumina. Paper, 69th LSA Annual Meeting, New Orleans. ERIC ED384231 (precursor of Grimes 2009 in Florey ed.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sound-correspondence and morphology comparison of Buru/Kayeli/Hukumina; stress mentioned only for Kayeli (enclitics extrametrical, 'not affecting penultimate stress on the root') and Buru; nothing on Hukumina stress; author notes he obtained 'very little reliable data' from the one Hukumina speaker.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 1991. The Buru language of Eastern Indonesia. PhD thesis, Australian National University. (hdl 1885/10925; scanned PDF, no text layer; scanned of pdf pp.3-14 and 46-53 = printed pp.26-33)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.28 (sec. 4.1): Hukumina 'phonology (both synchronic and diachronic), morphology, stress patterns and intonation contours are strikingly different from Buru, Kayeli, Sula, Ambelau, and the languages indigenous to Ambon' -- mentions stress but does NOT state where it falls. (Phonology chapter 5.2 is on Buru stress, penultimate; not Hukumina.)

sources.citation: Stokhof, W.A.L. (ed.) 1982. Holle lists: vocabularies in languages of Indonesia Vol.3/4: Central Moluccas: Ambon (II), Buru, Nusa Laut, Saparua. Pacific Linguistics D-50. Hukumina = list 55b (NBG 1896), pp.63-76.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. 'General information' gives only basic data (list 55b, 1896); wordlist diacritics (a-grave, i/o-macron, e-breve) are Holle vowel-quality/schwa marks per the Vol.1 conventions, not stress marks.

sources.citation: Stokhof, W.A.L. (ed.) 1980. Holle lists: vocabularies in languages of Indonesia Vol.1: Introductory volume. Pacific Linguistics D-17.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Transcription key pp.76-77: a-grave = Dutch 'man' [short a], i-macron = Dutch 'vier' [i], e-breve = schwa; the questionnaire's stress questions (16-17) belong to the 1931 edition only, so the 1896 Hukumina list carries no stress information.
